head: b4b7f9d5d02705912869be9e3d1a04889f5a5278
scope: PR 221, the pool line in claude-router status. A foreground lane router on port 18797 ran this code on Linux 7.0 x86_64, beside the daily router, with its state on the machine's ext4 disk (lane.py). Real accounts: copies of the dobby and work logins, with capacities 3 and 1, whose tokens expired more than 4.5 h later, read paid overflow, usage, and resets through the real API. The lane sent no request, because the change only draws a status line from readings the router already reports, and routing does not read it. lane.py recomputed the pool line from the lane's readings as CONTRACT.md's status row specifies and compared it with claude-router status on a pseudo-terminal at 100, 80, and 70 columns. Both accounts had used all of their weekly windows and none of their Fable windows, with weekly resets 4d 20h and 2d 12h away, so the live rows check capacity weighting of the tick but not of the fill. With stdout a pipe, status printed the account lines and no pool line. These two accounts have no 5-hour window, so the pool line fits at every width where the boxes draw. The Go tests named in CONTRACT.md check fill weighting, the 10-column rule, and the tie to the boxes. record.py built the record. Unchanged historical scenarios are references and were not rerun.

matrix.scenario: dobby token expires more than 4.5 h from now, outside the four-hour refresh lead
work token expires more than 4.5 h from now, outside the four-hour refresh lead
Lane code, executable, and SDK match the build at b4b7f9d and go.mod
Both lane accounts are signed in with paid overflow disabled and a usage reading at start
With no request sent, every limit reading comes from the usage read
At 100 columns, the pool line under the router line equals the capacity-weighted share left and even pace recomputed from the lane's readings

detail.method: lane.py's expected_pool_line computed the line from the lane's GET /claude-router/status readings, fetched just before and just after claude-router status ran on a pseudo-terminal with NO_COLOR=1, for both bracketing times: for each window, the sum of capacity times share left over the sum of capacity, and the same mean of each account's time to reset over the window's period, drawn in eighth-block cells with the tick at min(int(share x n + 0.5), n - 1). Both readings were the same. The printed line, the second line of the output, equals the computed line. The wk bar has 35 cells. dobby (capacity 3) resets in 4d 20h and work (capacity 1) in 2d 12h, so the weighted tick share is (3 x 0.6918 + 0.3585) / 4 = 0.6085, cell 21 from 0. An unweighted mean, 0.5251, would put it in cell 18.
